The model alias row becomes WITHDRAWN, not RESOLVED and not deleted: the gap was wrong, and the note says what disproved it (v1.0.80 resolves sonnet; the test agent had a typo). Both rows stay in the table, and no new rows are added.
assertions: Marks the git-subdir row MITIGATED, not RESOLVED, because Copilot still rejects git-subdir

evals.name: new-gaps-priority
evals.prompt: Three new ones for data/known-gaps.md. 1) Codex never runs a PreToolUse hook whose matcher uses | alternation, so our rm guard silently doesn't run there. 2) Copilot CLI's hook docs say a hook can set timeoutSec, but the shipped binary ignores it: hooks still run, always with the 30-second default. 3) Copilot CLI's /skills info cuts long descriptions off at 80 characters in its display; the skill itself works fine. Give me the rows.
evals.expected_output: Three new OPEN rows. The Codex matcher gap is HIGH: a guard hook silently not running is incorrect behavior. The Copilot timeoutSec gap is MED: hooks still work, but the docs disagree with the shipped binary. The /skills info truncation is LOW: cosmetic. Vendors are spelled as in the table (Codex, Copilot CLI). Each description says what goes wrong and what should happen instead (the hook should run for every tool the alternation names; timeoutSec should set the hook timeout, as documented; /skills info should show the whole description), with any workaround in the Status note rather than as the correct behavior.
assertions: Adds the Codex matcher gap as HIGH, with Vendor Codex and status OPEN
Adds the timeoutSec gap as MED (docs disagree with the shipped binary, but hooks still run), with Vendor Copilot CLI
Adds the /skills info truncation as LOW, with Vendor Copilot CLI
Each new row's description says what should happen instead, not only what goes wrong or a workaround
